component.name: Tessera
component.summary: Share smart card and token drivers with your other apps
Compartilhe os drivers de cartões e tokens com seus outros aplicativos

description.p: Tessera lets sandboxed apps use hardware tokens, smart cards and cloud certificates without installing any driver on the system. It runs the token drivers inside its own sandbox and shares every token with other apps through p11-kit, the standard way for Linux apps to reach PKCS#11 devices.
This is meant for immutable systems such as Fedora Silverblue, Kinoite, Bluefin, Aurora and Bazzite, where installing a vendor's driver package on the host is hard or impossible.

ul.li: Shows the card readers, the inserted tokens and their certificates
Drivers included: SafeSign IC, SafeNet Authentication Client and SerproID; more can be added as extensions
Vendor drivers are downloaded from the vendors at install time and checked against pinned checksums
Opens the vendors' tools, such as SafeSign's Token Administration and the SerproID app
Sets up Firefox, Chromium, Google Chrome, Brave and Papers to use the tokens, and shows the command that lets them reach Tessera
Publishes a driver only while it answers, so a driver that hangs cannot hang the apps
Keeps running in the background with an icon in the tray, and can start at login

description.p: Each driver runs in its own p11-kit server inside Tessera. Tessera adds them to the host's p11-kit configuration, and the host's p11-kit server (p11-kit-server.socket, enabled once) serves them to other apps. Sandboxed apps need --filesystem=xdg-run/p11-kit/pkcs11; PJeOffice Pro from FlatPark has it already.
The host needs pcscd with the CCID driver and p11-kit-server, which most distributions ship.

First release: one p11-kit server per driver (SafeSign IC, SafeNet Authentication Client, SerproID), published through the host p11-kit server; readers, tokens and certificates; set-up for Firefox, Chromium, Google Chrome, Brave and Papers; tray icon and start at login.
